title: Peoria Home Energy Rebates 2026: What We Confirmed and What We Could Not
desc: Peoria home energy rebates in 2026: free state weatherization and solar credits are confirmed, while Ameren Illinois rebate amounts could not be read. Peoria has the highest share of electric-heated homes of our Illinois cities.
lead: Peoria is served by Ameren Illinois for electricity and gas, and Ameren Illinois is the one big utility whose rebate amounts we could not read. Its rebate site blocked our reader on October 6, 2026, and we did not work around that. So this page lists what we did confirm, including free state weatherization and solar credit payments, and says clearly where we have no number. It also shows why Peoria's housing makes the free programs worth checking first.

sections:
The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey counts 54,010 homes in Peoria and 49,037 lived in year-round. Owners are 57.5% of households and renters 42.5%. Detached houses are 63.1% of homes, attached houses 4.8% and buildings of two to four homes 6.1%.

Homes are old: 69.0% were built before 1980, 20.4% before 1940 and 16.7% since 2000.

Electricity heats 31.0% of Peoria homes, the highest share among our four Illinois cities. Utility gas heats 67.2%, bottled gas 0.6% and fuel oil 0.1%. A household that heats with electric baseboards or a furnace with electric coils can cut its bill with a heat pump, if a rebate and a good installer make the numbers work. Ask Ameren Illinois what it pays before you buy.

For program year 2027 the state's income limit is $31,920 for one person, $43,280 for two, $54,640 for three and $66,000 for four. Eligible homes can get air sealing, insulation, heating repair or replacement and water heater work, up to $20,000 plus $4,000 for health and safety. Households that got help from the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program in the past 12 months qualify too.

Group A pays $70.37 per credit for a small home system in 2026-27, less than Group B's $80.77 in ComEd's area. That is a real gap, but solar savings also depend on your roof and your bill. Ask for the number of credits in writing. See our Illinois solar guide.

Renters are 42.5% of Peoria households, a larger share than in Naperville or Aurora. A tenant can ask the landlord to apply for weatherization, and the state program serves homes and apartments. Ask the landlord to look at the income limits before anyone signs a contract for new equipment. Keep any promise from a landlord in writing.
How we will update this page
When we or Ameren Illinois publish readable amounts we will add them with the date we read them. Until then, we would rather say we do not know than guess.
claim_heading: How to find money in Peoria
claim_steps: Check your income against the free weatherization limits and apply if you qualify.
Open AmerenIllinoisSavings.com in a normal browser and call Ameren Illinois to confirm any amount.
Ask three contractors to quote heat pumps and write the rebate as a separate line.
For solar, use an Illinois Shines approved vendor.
Keep every invoice and model number.
